critic: LEAD (independent critic, checked by a second agent)
verdict: The two shots without a person are close to the bar. The two shots of Dawn are not. cell_far is the film's shrinking cell: a small lit box under a cone that clearly narrows, about 40 px wide at the frame top and about 120 px where it meets the wall tops. bags is a worthy last image. It has a fine rim on the case handle, a hotspot that runs from about 73 graded at the pool's edge to 121 at its centre, and a gap between the two bags. cell_close has a real barred shaft and a barred patch on the floor. The beam in dawn now tapers as asked. But Dawn herself fails at final size. In dawn_high her right hand (frame left) still shows separated, fanned dark fingers against the lit floor. Her left hand (frame right) has three bright dots on its curled fingers in both Dawn shots: in dawn they peak at 129 graded on a hand whose median is about 22. Each sleeve ends in a pale bell cuff wider than the wrist. The trousers are straight now, but they read as stiff tubes on short legs. The visible leg split starts at about 43 % of her height, and the hem is a hard straight cut 4-5 cm off the floor with no break over the shoe. Hands and face (median 22-28) are darker than the cloth (36-46), which inverts the DECISIONS rule that the garment sits well below the stone skin. From the dawn camera the bun is hidden, so the top-lit hair reads as a flat cap on a broad-shouldered man (the uniform is the kit's men's casualsuit03). The cell is still a clean clay set. The steel unit's bowl reads as a waste bin, and the lower bunk is a black hole under the upper deck. The signs of occupancy that are there (books, a towel, folded greys, cups) are tidy and new, so nothing yet says twelve years. At the front of the bags pool, faint dark wandering streaks on the floor are foreshortened by the low lens into what looks like scribbled writing. As it stands, Ch 07 would not hold in a finished film.
answers:
These are the published frames at 4c5ff43 (frames/graded/void_stage, 1280x720), measured on the graded JPEGs and the raw PNGs. The code behind these five cameras has not changed since then. The newer additions (the chair, the seated Dawn in cell_far, dawn_close and the other new cameras) are not in these frames, so they are not judged here.

1. Hands: no, they do not read at final size. In dawn_high, enlarged, her right hand (frame left) shows three or four separated, fanned dark fingers against the lit floor, which reads as a claw. Her left hand (frame right) shows three bright dots on its curled fingers in both Dawn shots. In dawn there are 9 pixels above 90 graded and the peak is 129, on a hand whose median is 22. At 1280 the dots read as rings or glints. Both hands are nearly black: in dawn the left hand's median is about 28 and the right's 22, against cloth medians of 36-46. So they read as black gloves coming out of grey sleeves, not stone. The curled hands end near y 440, about 41 % of her height above the floor, which is a normal place for them. It is the low leg split (answer 3) that shortens the legs.

2. Sleeve cuffs: no. Each sleeve ends in a rounded bell that is wider than the forearm and lit from above. In dawn the frame-right arm is 13 px wide at y 345 and 23 px at the cuff (y 390). The cuffs are also the lightest part of the arm: about 40-50 graded at the cuff against about 35-40 higher up the arm. At 1280 they read as puffed lantern sleeves or rolled-up bunches, not a plain buttoned prison cuff, and their shadow leaves the hands black.

3. Trouser outline: only partly. The leggings problem is gone. Each leg is a straight tube, about 40 px (17 cm) at the thigh and 42-44 px at the hem, so there is no taper to the ankle. But shirt and trousers are one flat grey (UNIFORM uses one rgb, as the kit does), so the shirt hem does not read. The visible leg split starts at y 430, about 43 % of her 391 px height above the floor. A real inseam sits nearer 45-47 %, so the crotch looks dropped and the legs a little short. The hem is a hard horizontal cut about 10-12 px (4-5 cm) above the floor, with the dark shoe showing under it and no break over it. That reads as a stiff tube, not trousers resting on the shoe, though it is not high-waters. In dawn_high the legs read better.

4. Cell floor light: improved but not there. The patch is 183-192 graded against 125-140 for the floor around it (about 1.4:1, up from 1.2:1), and its six barred panes read. Four problems remain.
(a) The top spot's pool edge is a hard arc across the floor right under the shaft: at x 780 the floor jumps from 48 to 134 between y 470 and y 500. That reads as a stage spotlight edge inside the room.
(b) The shaft shows only over the dark floor behind that arc and dies at it, 80-100 px above the patch, so shaft and patch still do not visibly join.
(c) The window glass (p90 130, max 154) is darker than the patch it throws (about 190), so the source reads dimmer than its light. The pane already glows (frosted_glow at strength 2.0), but too weakly.
(d) The window seems to have a horizontal crossbar with a second, lower row of panes, while the patch is one row. That lower row is not glass. It is the lit splayed sill, showing between the bars under the pane's bottom rail. The patch is physically right, but the window reads as two rows.
The panes' left end also sits on the bunk's black shadow (about 21-25 graded), and with their uniform razor-sharp edges the panes read like six paper cards laid on the floor. In cell_far the same patch (217) against the floor (142) reads well.

5. Taper of the beam: yes in dawn, dawn_high and cell_far. Widths are measured where the haze stands 4 code values above the black. Dawn's haze is about 260 px wide at the frame top, 350 at y 240, 370 at y 300 and about 460 just above the floor (about 1.8:1). It reads as a cone coming down out of the dark, not a curtain. dawn_high goes from about 210 to 310 px over its top 300 rows. cell_far goes from about 40 px at the frame top to about 120 px where it meets the wall tops. Caveat: the beam is a ghost, peaking at 27-31 graded over a background of 2-3. That is only about 25 code values spread over hundreds of pixels, so the YouTube encode is likely to band it into steps; the grade's fine grain is all that protects it. In bags the haze is a broad 700-750 px glow that barely changes width. That works as a backdrop, but it is not a beam.

fixes.problem: The hands are still the failing human detail. In dawn_high her right hand (frame left) shows three or four separated, fanned dark fingers with lit floor between them. Her left hand (frame right) has three bright dots on its curled fingers in both shots; in dawn they peak at 129 graded (9 pixels above 90) on a hand whose median is about 22. Both hands are darker than the cloth (22-28 against 36-46), so they read as black gloves.
fixes.fix: (a) void_stage_fit.close_hands closes the fingers with its converge loop. Each finger is turned about the palm normal to `converge` (1.0 deg) of its neighbour, capped at 20 deg. FINGER_GAP is not used there, and _close_on drives only the thumb. Read the 'VOID hands:' log line for side R. If a pair's splay stays well above +1 deg, or its turn hit the 20-degree cap, raise the cap to about 30 deg and converge to 3-4 deg for R, keeping min_gap. Repeat until no floor shows between the fingers in dbg_dawn_high. (b) The dots are most likely the tops of the curled finger joints catching the lamp below the cuff's shadow. hands_stone now mixes only Base Color by handmask. Use the same mask to drive Specular IOR Level 0.3 -> 0.08 and Roughness 0.66 -> 0.85. If the dots remain, cut the middle-joint curl (the second value in CURL) by about a third. (c) Lift the hands out of black. Add an area light 'hand_return', 0.6 x 0.4 m and about 30 W, at (D.x, D.y - 1.4, 0.5), aimed at (D.x, D.y, 0.8), and link it to the body only with st.link_lights. Targets: hand median about 50-60 graded, no hand pixel above 1.6x that median, and the bowed face still in shadow (no speck on the nose tip). Check both hands in dbg_dawn and dbg_dawn_high.

fixes.problem: The sleeve cuffs flare into pale bells wider than the wrist (13 px forearm against 23 px cuff in dawn), and they are the brightest part of the arm.
fixes.fix: In void_stage_fit.loosen_suit, after the shirt pass, take the sleeve vertices (the 'sleeve' set) within 8 cm of the DEF-hand head on each side. Clamp their radial distance from the forearm axis (DEF-forearm.X.001 head to DEF-hand head) to the forearm skin radius + 10 mm. Pull the last 1.5 cm in to + 6 mm, so the cuff closes round the wrist like a buttoned band, and keep the 'margin' check after it. Then darken the cuff top: multiply Base Color by about 0.75 on suit vertices within 6 cm of the cuff edge, using a vertex-colour mask like 'handmask'. The net on the whole suit is handled in the priority-3 light fix. Target: the cuff at or below the upper-arm value.

fixes.problem: The trousers read as stiff tubes on short legs. Shirt and trousers are one grey, so the shirt hem does not read. The visible leg split starts at y 430, about 43 % of her 391 px height above the floor; a real inseam sits nearer 45-47 %. The hem is a hard straight cut about 10-12 px (4-5 cm) above the floor, with the dark shoe showing under it and no break.
fixes.fix: Keep the uniform one grey. It is the kit's colour (the people.dawn_prison tint), and DECISIONS keep one outfit across the courtroom, Void Stage and visiting room, so a two-tone split here would break continuity. (1) Make the shirt hem read by its form: raise loosen_suit hem_lift from 0.015 to 0.03, so the untucked hem stands off the hips and draws a thin shadow line under the top light. (2) In the legs pass, ramp the hem vertices down along u, from t 0.85 to the hem, by up to 0.02-0.03 m. Go no further, because the hem is only 4-5 cm up now. The back of the hem should end about 2 cm off the floor and the front should rest on the instep. Double the break ripple from 0.0042 to 0.008 so a soft ring stacks above the shoe. Then re-run fit.shoe_fit and fit.clearance, and check that no hem vertex goes below the soles.

fixes.problem: Seen from the front, the bun is hidden behind the bowed head, so the top-lit hair reads as a flat cap. With the square shoulders of the men's uniform shirt and the wide trousers, the figure reads as a man in a cap, not Dawn.
fixes.fix: Show the bun in silhouette. Set DAWN_TURN 18 -> 32 and POSE['head'] (28, 3) -> (28, -6). The head then turns back toward the lens while the body stands three-quarter on, and the bun clears the skull outline against the beam. Then give the bun a thin rim: a copy of spot_dawn at 0.4 power, linked to the '_bun' mesh only. Check in dbg_dawn that a bun shape stands at least 6 px off the back of the head at 1280.

fixes.problem: In the near band of the pool (y 565-595), faint dark wandering streaks are foreshortened into squiggles that look like faint handwriting. They sit in the film's final image. All the marks are darker than the floor (in the raw frame 793 pixels fall more than 8 below the local floor and none rise above it). So they are most likely the floor shader's heel and case-wheel streaks (the ridged-noise term dk, mixed toward 0.04), not the spike tape, which is mixed lighter (0.105 over a 0.086 floor).
fixes.fix: The floor material is built in void_stage_set.stage_floor() (floor() only makes the mesh). Give stage_floor a second centre, the bags island G, and fade both the dk streaks and the tape mask to zero within about 1.6 m of it (the bags pool is 1.15 m in radius). Use a distance mask on the Geometry position, like the cell's near-black mask. If the streaks are wanted elsewhere, straighten dk instead, with a weaker meander. Check the front band (y 560-595) of bags at 1280 for any letter-like mark.

fixes.problem: The shaft and the patch still do not join. The back edge of the cell pool is a hard arc (48 -> 134 graded within 30 px) right under the shaft, and the shaft disappears at that arc 80-100 px above the patch. The pane (max 154) is darker than its patch (about 190). The lit splayed sill between the bars under the pane's bottom rail reads as a second row of glass, which the one-row patch does not match.
fixes.fix: (a) Raise SPOTS['cell'] blend from 0.25 to 0.5, so the back edge of the pool rolls off over about 40 cm instead of an arc. Re-check the cell_far sliver afterwards. (b) In build_cell_island, add a second, denser haze_box_along (density about 0.14). Run it from the point on the window ray 0.6 m above the floor down to the patch. Add it to the top spot's exclude list (st.link_lights([main, hot], exclude=[shaft, low_shaft])), so the shaft shows over the lit floor all the way to the panes. (c) The pane already emits (frosted_glow 'slot pane', strength 2.0 in st.cell). Raise it to about 5-6, so the glass lands near 210-220 graded, above the patch. (d) Let the sill's sloped face fall darker: give it the dark paint instead of the raw section material, or keep it out of cell_window_light. The slot then reads as the one row of glass it is, matching the patch.

fixes.problem: The frames are dim. Dawn's frame maximum is 145 graded (the crown), and the pool runs from about 85 at its edge to 125 at its centre, so the lit island reads grey rather than lit. The garment (36-46) is lighter than the hands and face (22-28), which inverts the DECISIONS rule that the cloth sits well below the stone.
fixes.fix: Raise SPOTS['dawn'] watts from 4600 to 6400 (+0.5 stop). Scale the cloth and hair nets down by the same factor so they stay where they are: in light_suit, net 0.42 -> 0.30 and hair_net 0.28 -> 0.20. Leave body_net at 0.75, so the stone rises half a stop with the pool. Cut bounce_w on the suit from 80 to 45 W, and let the hand_return light (priority-1 fix) lift the hands. Targets: pool centre roughly 145-160 graded, crown no brighter than now, cloth median about 0.7x the hands'.

fixes.problem: The shirt's bump (the BANDS wave in prison_suit: scale 6, distortion 7, bump strength 0.35) reads at final size as even horizontal stripes across the chest and upper arms, like corrugated card, not cotton folds.
fixes.fix: In prison_suit, cut the fold Bump strength from 0.35 to 0.12 and the wave scale from 6 to 3.5. Instead, raise creases() (a displacement on the whole suit) from strength 0.010 to 0.014 and lower its stretch from 3.2 to about 1.5. A few irregular folds then come from geometry, at the inner elbow, under the bust and at the waist.

fixes.problem: The cell is still a clean set. The stainless unit is a combination unit (cabinet with an inset basin, tap and push button, the bowl on a pedestal), but the bowl, an upright straight-sided oval on a square pedestal, reads as a waste bin, and the basin is lost in shadow. Under the upper deck the lower bunk is a black hole (median about 24 graded), and the lower blanket is a stiff wavy sheet. The signs of occupancy that are there (books on the desk, a towel on the rail, folded greys on the shelf, cups) are tidy and new, so nothing reads as twelve years.
fixes.fix: (1) The unit is built in void_stage_set.combo_unit. Taper the bowl's side so it narrows toward the pedestal (create_cone radius1 about 0.7 of radius2), and merge the pedestal into a rounded-front skirt, so it reads as a toilet. Let the basin rim in the cabinet top catch the spot. (2) The mattress vinyl is already at (0.10, 0.11, 0.12) and still goes black, because the upper deck shades the lower bunk from the top spot. Add a weak area light (about 0.8 x 0.4 m, 10-15 W, low on the open side, aimed in under the deck), linked only to the lower mattress, pillow and blanket. Target: the mattress lip near 70-80 graded. The newer bunk_floor_return light is linked to the seated Dawn only. (3) Give the lower blanket a straight hem and 3-4 vertical folds. (4) Add wear rather than more cups: a tied bundle of plain envelopes (0.11 x 0.22 m, warm off-white at value 0.45, no marks) beside the books, softened book corners, and a worn, pilled patch on the blanket.

fixes.problem: A thin grey sliver (graded up to about 60 at y 510-513, x 592-655) still lies on the void floor about 10 px under the slab's front edge.
fixes.fix: Pull the cell pool's front edge in: shrink pool ry from 1.85 to 1.78, or move its aim 5 cm toward +y. Or, in void_stage_set.stage_floor(cell=...), start the near-black mask closer to the slab on the -Y side. It now fades in only from |dy| > 2.35 m, and the slab's front face is at 1.86 m. Check at 1280 that no pixel below the slab rises above 12 graded.
